We call a tuple $(N,\ket{\psi})$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_1\otimes \cdots\otimes \mH_r$ is an entangled state on the joint space of all $r$ players, and $N$ a collection of POVM for each player and possible question to the player, a \emph{strategy} for the players in $G$. Note that we may always assume $\ket{\psi}$ is a pure state and all POVM are projective. 

Given a game $G$ we denote by $\omega^*(G)$ the highest probability of winning that can be achieved by $r$ players sharing quantum entanglement. For a more thorough introduction to nonlocal games in a similar framework as used here we refer to e.g.~\cite{ji2015classical}. 

One of our tests uses nonlocal games as a means to enforce anticommutation relations between a player's observables. Towards this we introduce the following definition. 

\begin{definition}[Anticommutation game]\label{def:ac-game}
Let $\wg\in (0,1]$ and $\delta:[0,1]\to [0,1]$ a continuous function such that $\delta(0)=0$. 
A two-player game $G$ is called a $(\wg,\delta)$ anticommutation game if
$\omega^*(G)\geq \wg$ and moreover there exists questions $q_X,q_Z$ (called
\emph{special questions}) to the second player and $\{\pm1\}$-valued functions $f_X,f_Z$ defined on the player's set of possible answers to questions $q_X,q_Z$ respectively such that the following two properties hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item {\em Completeness:} There exists a strategy using the state
$\ket{\EPR}_{AB}^{\ot m}$ for some $m \geq 1$ and projective measurements that achieves the optimal success probability $\wg$, and is uch that measurement operators $\{A_q^a\}
\in \Pos(\mH_A)$ for the second player satisfy $\sum_a f_X(a) A_{a_X}^a = \sigma_X \ot \Id$ and $\sum_a f_Z(a) A_{q_Z}^a
= \sigma_Z \ot \Id$, where $\sigma_X$ and $\sigma_Z$ act on
the first EPR pair and the identity on the remaining EPR pairs. Moreover,
for every quesion $q$ received by the second player and answer $a$, the projector $A_q^a$ can be written as
$A_q^a = \sum_j \Pi_j$ where each $\Pi_j$ is the projector onto an eigenspace of
a tensor product of $\sigma_X, \sigma_Z$ and $\Id$.\footnote{This seemingly ad-hoc condition is needed for the use of the anticommutation game in the Hamiltonian self-test described in Section~\ref{sec:manyprovers}, but not in the Pauli braiding test from Section~\ref{sec:twoprover}.} We call such a strategy an
\emph{honest strategy} for $G$.
\item
Soundness: Let a projective strategy for the players in $G$ be given such that the strategy uses entangled state $\ket{\psi}\in\mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ and measurement operators $\{A_q^a\} \in\Pos(\mH_A)$ for the second player. Then for any $\eps>0$, provided the strategy has success probability at least $\wg-\eps$ in $G$, there exists 
 isometries $U:\mH_A \to \C^2\otimes \mH_{A'}$ and $V:\mH_B \to \C^2 \otimes \mH_{B'}$ and a state $\ket{\psi'}\in\mH_{A'}\otimes \mH_{B'}$ such that if 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-ac-xz}
X = \sum_a f_X(a) A_{q_X}^a\qquad \text{and}\qquad Z = \sum_a {f_Z(a)} A_{q_Z}^a
\end{equation}
then 
$$ \big\| U\otimes V \ket{\psi} - \ket{\EPR}\otimes \ket{\psi'} \big\|\leq \delta\; \text{and}\;
\max\Big\{ \DIS_{\rho}(X,U^\dagger (\sigma_X\otimes \Id_{A'}) U),\,
\DIS_{\rho}(Z,V^\dagger (\sigma_Z\otimes \Id_{B'}) V)\Big\}\leq \delta.$$
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

The CHSH game~\cite{CHSH69} and the Mermin-Peres Magic Square game~\cite{mermin1990simple,peres1990incompatible} are both known to be anti-commutation games. For the former, see e.g.~\cite{McKagueYS12rigidity} and for the latter,~\cite{wu2016device,CN16}. The advantage of the CHSH game is that there is an optimal strategy which only requires a single EPR pair of entanglement. The Magic Square has the advantage of having value $1$, but an optimal strategy requires two EPR pairs. 

\begin{lemma}
The CHSH game is a $(\cos^2 \pi/8,O(\sqrt{\eps}))$ anticommutation game. 
The Magic Square game is a $(1,O(\sqrt{\eps}))$ anticommutation game. 
\end{lemma}

%A fact that will be relevant later is that for both game there exists an optimal
%strategy for the players which only requires the measurement of $\sigma_X$ and
%$\sigma_Z$ Pauli observables, as well as (for the case of CHSH) $(\sigma_X \pm
%\sigma_Z)/\sqrt{2}$.

%----------------------%
\section{The linearity test}
\label{sec:linearity}
%----------------------%

We state and analyze a variant of the classic 3-query linearity test of Blum, Luby, and Rubinfeld~\cite{BLR93} (BLR) that can be played with two entangled players. The two-player test is based on the idea of oracularization with a dummy question introduced in~\cite{IKM09}.  Our analysis builds on~\cite{IV12}, who analyze a $3$-player variant. Their proof is an extension of the Fourier-analytic proof due to H{\aa}stad to the matrix-valued setting. We analyze the two-player variant using similar techniques. 

We note that the use of two players, rather than three as in
the original test, is essential for our applications to
self-testing. Ultimately we will require the provers to succeed in a linearity test performed in either of two mutually incompatible bases (e.g. the $X$ and $Z$ bases). Two provers
can achieve this by sharing a maximally entangled state, but there is no {tripartite} state that would allow three entangled provers to obtain consistent answers whenever they measure their share of the state in either the $X$ or the $Z$ basis. (Formulated differently, $\sigma_X\otimes \sigma_X$ and $\sigma_Z\otimes \sigma_Z$ share a common $+1$ eigenvector, the EPR pair; $\sigma_X\otimes \sigma_X \otimes \sigma_X$ and $\sigma_Z\otimes \sigma_Z \otimes \sigma_Z$ do not. This is a manifestation of entanglement monogamy.)

We show the result in two
steps. First we show that any set of quantum observables satisfying
linearity relations approximately in expectation can be ``rounded'' to a
nearby set of observables satisfying these relations exactly. 

\begin{theorem}
  Suppose there exist observables $\{A(a)\}_{a\in
  \{0,1\}^n}$ in $\Obs(\mH)$ acting on a state
  $\rho \in \Density(\mH)$ such that 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:qblr-0}
	\E_{a, b} \Trho\big( A(a) A(b) A(a+b)\big) \geq 1-\delta.
	\end{equation}
	Then there exists an extended state $\rho' = \rho \otimes
  \proj{\rm{anc}} \in \Density(\mH\otimes \mH')$ and observables $\{\cA(a)\}$ in $\Obs(\mH\otimes\mH')$ such that 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:qblr-1}
	\cA(a) \cA(b) = \cA(a+b) \quad \forall a, b \in \{0, 1\}^n\qquad \text{and}\qquad \E_a
  \DIS_{\rho'} (\cA(a), A(a))^2 \leq\delta.
	\end{equation}
\label{thm:qblr}
\end{theorem}

Here, and throughout this paper, the notation $a + b$ denotes the
bitwise XOR of $a$ and $b$, i.e. the sum of $a$ and $b$ viewed
as elements of the additive group ${\mathbb{Z}}_2^n$. We call observables
$\{\cA(a)\}$ satisfying the first set of relations in~\eqref{eq:qblr-1} \emph{exactly linear}.

\begin{proof}
For every $u\in\{0,1\}^n$ consider the Fourier transform  $\hat{A}^u =
\E_{a} (-1)^{a\cdot u} A(a)$. Define measurement operators
  $B^u = (\hat{A}^u)^2$.
By Parseval's identity, these operators form a POVM. Using Naimark's theorem there exists an ancilla space $\mH'$, $\proj{\rm anc}\in\Density(\mH')$, and a projective
measurement $\{C^u\}$ on $\mH\otimes \mH'$ that simulates $\{B^u\}$. Introduce 
observables
\[ \cA(a) = \sum_{u} (-1)^{u\cdot a} C^u. \]
From the orthogonality of the projectors $C^u$ it follows that $\cA(a)
\cA(b) = \cA(a+b)$. Write 
\begin{align*}
  \E_{a} \CON_{\rho'}(A(a), \cA(a))
  &= \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\E_{a}\Re\Tr_{\rho'}\big( A(a)\cA(a)\big)\\
	&= \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\E_{a}\Re\Big(\sum_u \Trho\big( (-1)^{u\cdot a} A(a)(\hat{A}^u)^2\big)\Big)\\
	&= \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\sum_u \Trho\big((\hat{A}^u)^3\big).
\end{align*}
To conclude, note that
  $\sum_u \Trho((\hat{A}^u)^3) =\E_{ab} \Trho(A(a) A(b) A(a + b))$, and use the assumption made in the theorem and the relation between $\CON_{\rho'}$ and $\DIS_{\rho'}^2 $.
\end{proof}

Next we exhibit a two-player game such that any strategy which succeeds with
probability at least $1 - \eps$ in the game must satisfy the assumption~\eqref{eq:qblr-0} of
Theorem~\ref{thm:qblr} for some $\delta = O(\sqrt{\eps})$.

\begin{figure}[H]
\rule[1ex]{16.5cm}{0.5pt}\\
The verifier performs the following one-round interaction with two
players. He starts by choosing one of the players at random and
labels her Alice; the other player is labeled Bob. In each test each player is sent a pair of $n$-bit strings. The $n$-bit strings are always assumed to be sent in lexicographic order.  
\begin{enumerate}
\item Choose two strings $a,b \in \{0,1\}^n$ uniformly at random. Send $(a,b)$ to Alice.
\item Let $c$ be with equal
  probability either $a$, $b$, or $a+b$, and let $c'\in\{0,1\}^n$ be chosen uniformly at random. Send $(c,c')$ to Bob.
	\item The players reply with $\alpha,\beta\in\{\pm 1\}$ and $\gamma,\gamma'\in\{\pm 1\}$ respectively. Depending on the value of $c$ the verifier performs one of the following two tests:
	\begin{enumerate}
        \item
          \emph{Consistency test}: if $c = a$ (resp. $b$), accept if and only if both players return the same value as their answer to that question: $\gamma=\alpha$ (resp. $\gamma=\beta$).
        \item
          \emph{Linearity test}: if $c = a + b$, accept if and only if $\gamma = \alpha \beta$.
        \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\rule[1ex]{16.5cm}{0.5pt}\\
\caption{The two-player linearity test}
\label{fig:linearity}
\end{figure}

  whose elements are given by $\tilde{M}_{a}^{\a} := \E_{b}
  \sum_{\beta} M_{a,b}^{\a,\beta}$, and let $\{A_a^\a\}_{\a} \in \Pos(\mH_A \otimes \mH_{A'})$ be the
  projective measurement obtained by Naimark dilation of $\tilde{M}$.
	
	Then the
  observables $A(a) := A_a^{0} - A_a^{1}$ satisfy 
	$$\E_{a,b} \Tr_{\rho'}(A(a) A(b) A(a+b)) =
  1-O(\sqrt{\eps}),$$
	where $\rho' = \proj{\psi}\otimes \proj{\rm anc}_{\mH_{A'}}$.
  \label{thm:qblr_game}
\end{theorem}


\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:qblr_game}]
Introduce the following conditional measurement operator on $\mH_B$,
\begin{align*}
  N_{a|a b}^{\a} &= \sum_{\beta} N_{ab}^{\a \beta}.
\end{align*}
Note that for every $a,b$ and $\a$, $N_{a|ab}^\a$ is a projector since we assumed each $M_{ab}^{\a \beta}$ is as well. 
Suppose that the players' acceptance probability conditioned on the verifier performing the consistency part of the test (i.e. $c=a$ or $c=b$) is $1 -
\eps_{c}$, while conditioned on the verifier performing the linearity part of the test (i.e. $c=a+b$) it is $1 -

\section{At a glance}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The source quotes a fiberwise consequence
  of a state-dependent quantum linearity theorem, but suppresses two averages
  and a compatibility argument for the auxiliary spaces.
  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} One faithful theorem for a single family,
  followed by a finite common-extension construction that makes the auxiliary space
  uniform over the outer parameters.
  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Finite direct sums, extensions of
  operators, and squared norms are standard linear algebra.  The imported
  quantum linearity theorem and its state-dependent metric are project-level
  inputs.
  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Theorem~10 of
  \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}, finite averaging, and extension by the identity
  on orthogonal summands.  This reduction is tracked in
  \ghissue{19}.
\end{itemize}

\section{Key theorem forms}

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\rho$ be an arbitrary
density operator on $H$, and let $u\mapsto O^u$ be binary observables on $H$,
indexed by $\mathbb F_2^t$.  The cited theorem assumes the averaged
correlation estimate
\[
  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u,v}
  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left(O^u O^v O^{u+v}\rho\right) \geq 1-\delta.
\]
It produces an auxiliary space $H'$, a unit vector $\mathrm{anc}\in H'$, and
binary observables $L^u$ on $H\otimes H'$ satisfying, with
$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}|$,
\[
  L^uL^v=L^{u+v}
  \quad\text{for every }u,v.
\]
Moreover,
\[
  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})^\dagger
    (L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})\,\rho'\right)\leq\delta.
\]
In particular, $L^0=I$: exact linearity gives $(L^0)^2=L^0$, while an
observable is invertible.

The chapter needs a parameterized version.  For each pair $(x,z)$ it applies
the theorem to $(r,s)\mapsto O^{x,z,r,s}$.  Since the provider theorem accepts
the actual nonnegative defect on each fiber, no assumption that a fiber defect
is at most one, and no good--bad fiber split, is needed.  One must still
formulate the finite common-extension step that makes the auxiliary space
uniform over $(x,z)$.

\section{Comparison with the quoted statement}

Lines~711--725 of
\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} quote the
linearity theorem.  The displayed hypothesis correctly averages over both
group variables.  The displayed conclusion, however, says that the corrected
observable is close for every $u$, whereas Theorem~10 of the cited work gives
closeness only on average over $u$ \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  The quotation
also inserts $\delta\leq1$, which is absent from the provider theorem and would
unnecessarily obstruct applying it with a fiber's actual defect.  The assertion
at the identity follows from exact linearity as above.

Lines~825--832 construct the family $O^{x,z,r,s}$ and establish approximate
linearity only after averaging over $x,z,r,r',s,s'$.  They then apply the
single-family theorem separately for every $(x,z)$ and state that sufficiently
many zero ancillas avoid a further extension.  The remaining implicit step is
to make the theorem's possibly fiber-dependent auxiliary spaces uniform.

The finite setting admits a standard repair.  Apply the theorem on each fiber
with its actual defect, choose one finite auxiliary space large enough for all
returned spaces, and embed each returned space so that its unit vector maps to
one fixed vector.  Extend the conjugated observables by the identity on the
orthogonal complement.  The embeddings may depend on the fiber because the
observables do.  Averaging then yields the conclusion used later in the
chapter.  This is an open reduction, not a counterexample to the quoted theorem
or to the source's eventual combined-measurement conclusion.

\section{Blueprint and formalization status}

Theorem~\path{thm:linearity} and
Remark~\path{rem:linearity-import} in
\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex} record respectively the
averaged provider theorem and the common-ancilla obligation for its fiberwise
use.  The relevant material is at lines~98--147 and 149--191 of that chapter.

The declaration \path{exists_exactly_linear_observables} in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean} assumes a nonnegative defect, a
positive semidefinite trace-one operator, binary observables, and the averaged
three-observable correlation.  It returns one finite ancillary space and
normalized ancillary vector for that family, exactly linear binary observables
on the extension, and only the averaged squared-distance bound with the same
defect.  It neither assumes $\delta\leq1$ nor asserts pointwise closeness.  Its
statement therefore matches the provider-faithful blueprint theorem rather
than the strengthened quotation in the QPBT paper.  Its proof remains open,
and no Lean declaration yet supplies the finite common-extension construction
for the family indexed by $(x,z)$.

Issue~\#19 introduced this discrepancy record for the extraction skeleton;
\ghissue{47} owns the Stage~4.3 proof work consumed downstream.  The chapter-16
extraction declarations consume the concrete \path{GlobalPairWitness}; they
do not assume a new fiberwise linearity hypothesis or a common ancillary space.

\section{Conclusion}

The primary discrepancy is a quantifier mismatch in the quotation: the cited
linearity theorem gives average, not pointwise, closeness.  Its use for the
family indexed by $(x,z)$ also requires an explicit finite common-extension
argument.  Both are open formal reductions compatible with the intended
source conclusion.

\section{Key theorem forms}

Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
\[
  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).

Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
\[
  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
  \qquad
  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
\]
Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
\[
  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
\]
Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.

For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
\[
  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
\]
not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
$\Delta$.

\[
  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
\]
where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.

This transfer is an open proof obligation for the next extraction stage.  It
must be a theorem derived from the concrete swap unitaries, transformed-state
estimate, and operator comparisons.  It must not be stored as a bridge field,
residual assumption, or hypothesis of the source-labelled soundness theorem.

\section{Blueprint and formalization status}

The proof of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} and the soundness proof in
\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} use the corrected
positive-contraction estimate, make the small-error case distinction explicit,
and isolate the range-projection calculation.  The chapter therefore preserves
the source's state and observable conclusions while exposing the omitted
argument.

The structure \path{ExtractionWitness} in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/Unitary.lean} contains only the two-sided
unitarity equations for the concrete swap maps, a normalized auxiliary state,
the transformed-state estimate, and the two-player Pauli-projector comparison.
The theorem \path{exists_extractionWitness} concludes the existence of this
data at the explicit extraction scale from the projective strategy and its
\path{GlobalPairWitness}; it assumes no range-projection transfer, bridge, or
residual package.  Thus these declarations match the Stage~4.2 extraction
lemma, including the corrected numerical estimates, but do not formalize the
later passage to the isometries in the soundness theorem.  No declaration yet
states that passage.

Issue~\#19 owns this concrete Stage~4.2 interface and discrepancy record.
\ghissue{47} owns the Stage~4.3 proof of
\path{exists_extractionWitness} and the separate range-projection theorem
needed by \path{pauli_soundness}; that theorem must be derived from the
concrete data rather than stored in the witness.

\section{Conclusion}

The printed triangle calculation has repairable numerical errors, and the
last passage from unitaries to isometries omits a genuine range-projection
argument.  Neither defect is a counterexample to Pauli soundness.  The former
is corrected by positive-contraction inequalities and a small-error split;
the latter remains a named downstream proof obligation whose hypotheses are
already supplied by the extraction lemma.

 /-- `δ_qld = O(δ_S^{1/4} + md/q)` of lem:qld-unitary, as an explicit functional. -/
 noncomputable def deltaExtract (C deltaS : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   C * (deltaS ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) + ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))
 
 /-- lem:qld-unitary (qpbt-paper 14_…tex:1666-1685): the swap unitaries of
 def:v-swap-unitary extract the EPR state and the Pauli observables. -/
 structure ExtractionWitness (S : ExpandedSetting P ε) (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaS)
     (delta : ℝ) where
   aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Pair × Pair)                 -- registers AA'BB'
   aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   state_close : ‖swapBoth w S.psiHat - idealExpState aux‖ ^ 2 ≤ delta
   pauli_close : ∀ (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind),
     opFamilyDistSq (Distribution.dirac ())
       (fun _ (h : Reg) =>
         conjBy (placeSide side (swapUnitary w))
           (placeSide side (onA ((S.pauliMeasRaw W).effect h))))
       (fun _ (h : Reg) => placeRegPP side (pauliProj W h))
       (idealExpState aux) ≤ delta
 
 theorem exists_extractionWitness :
     ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) [FieldModel P.q] (ε deltaS : ℝ)
       (S : ExpandedSetting P ε) (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaS),
       Nonempty (ExtractionWitness S w (deltaExtract C deltaS P.m P.d P.q)) := by

   832	\subsection{Polynomials and the low-degree code}
   833	\label{sec:ld-encoding}
   834	
   835	In this section, we introduce some basic definitions about polynomials over finite fields. 
   836	An $m$-variate polynomial $f$ over $\F_q$ is a function of the form
   837	\[
   838		f(x_1,\ldots,x_m) = \sum_{\alpha \in \{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}^m} c_\alpha
   839	  x_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots x_m^{\alpha_m}
   840	\]
   841	where $\{c_\alpha\}$ is a collection of coefficients in $\F_q$.
   842	We say that $f$ has \emph{individual degree (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha\neq 0$ only if
   843	$\alpha_i \leq d $ for all $1\leq i\leq m$, and that it has \emph{total degree
   844	  (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha\neq 0$ only if $\sum_i \alpha_i \leq d$.
   845	(Affine) \emph{multilinear} polynomials are polynomials with individual degree
   846	$1$.
   847	
   848	Low-degree polynomials play an important role in this paper.
   849	For one, the classical and quantum low-degree tests of \Cref{sec:ldt} are
   850	nonlocal games that efficiently certify that the players' answers are consistent
   851	with low-degree polynomials.
   852	Low-degree polynomials are also crucial in the probabilistically checkable
   853	proofs (PCP) construction that are used in ``answer reduction'' transformation
   854	(\Cref{sec:ans}).
   855	
   856	We recall the Schwartz-Zippel lemma: 
   857	
   858	\begin{lemma}[Schwartz-Zippel lemma~\cite{Sch80,Zip79}]
   859	  \label{lem:schwartz-zippel}
   860	  Let $f, g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ be two unequal polynomials with total degree at most $d$. Then
   861	  \begin{equation*}
   862	    \Pr_{x \sim \F_q^m}[f(x) = g(x)] \leq d/q\;.
   863	  \end{equation*}
   864	\end{lemma}
   865	
   866	
   867	\paragraph{The low-degree code.}
   868	The Schwartz-Zippel lemma implies that the set of low-degree polynomials form an
   869	error-correcting code with good distance, which we call the \emph{low-degree
   870	  code}.\footnote{It is also known as the \emph{generalized Reed-Muller code} in
   871	  the coding theory literature.}
   872	
   873	Fix an integer $m \in \N$ and let $M = 2^m$.
   874	For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ define the following $m$-variate multilinear
   875	polynomial over $\F_q$:
   876	\[
   877		\ind_{m,y}(x) = \prod_{i: y_i = 1} x_i \cdot \prod_{i: y_i = 0} (1 - x_i) \;.
   878	\]
   879	Here, we identify $\{0,1\}$ as a subset of $\F_q$.
   880	Notice that, when restricted to the subcube $\{0,1\}^m$, $\ind_{m, y}$ is zero
   881	everywhere except for when $x = y$.
   882	For $a\in \F_q^M$, label the coordinates of $a$ as $a_y$ for $y\in \{0,1\}^m$
   883	(identifying the latter set with $\{1,\ldots,M\}$ using, say, the lexicographic
   884	ordering on strings).
   885	For any such $a$ define the multilinear polynomial $g_a: \F_q^m \to \F_q$,
   886	called the \emph{low-degree encoding of $a$}, as follows:
   887	\begin{equation}
   888	\label{eq:ld-encoding}
   889		 g_a(x) = \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} a_y \cdot \ind_{m,y}(x)\;.
   890	\end{equation}
   891	Note that for any $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, $g_a(y) = a_y$.
   892	Furthermore, the map $a\mapsto g_a$ is linear: for every $x \in \F_q^m$,
   893	\begin{equation}
   894	\label{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}
   895		g_a(x) = a \cdot \ind_m(x)\;,
   896	\end{equation}
   897	where $\ind_m(x)$ is the vector $(\ind_{m,y}(x))_{y \in \{0,1\}^m}\in\F_q^M$.
   898	
   899	\begin{lemma}
   900	\label{lem:ld-encoding-complexity}
   901	Let $q$ be an admissible field size, and let $M = 2^m$ for some integer $m$.
   902	The complexity of computing the evaluation of the low-degree encoding $g_a(x)$,
   903	given $a \in \F_q^M$ and $x \in \F_q^m$ represented in binary, is $\poly(M,\log
   904	q)$.
   905	\end{lemma}
   906	\begin{proof}
   907		Computing $g_a(x)$ requires computing the sum of products $a_y \cdot
   908	  \ind_{m,y}(x)$ over all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$.
   909	  Via \Cref{lem:efficient_arithmetic}, evaluating $\ind_{m,y}(x)$ takes time
   910	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ because it requires performing $m$ multiplications of $\F_q$
   911	  elements, and therefore the product $a_y \cdot \ind_{m,y}(x)$ requires
   912	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ time.
   913	  Computing the sum over all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ requires $M \cdot \poly(m,\log q)
   914	  = \poly(M,\log q)$ time, as claimed.
   915	\end{proof}

    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The source applies a decoder--encoder
    23	  identity to every bounded individual-degree polynomial, although the identity
    24	  is guaranteed for encoded polynomials and can fail outside the encoding image.
    25	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} One restricted algebraic identity and one
    26	  probabilistic estimate showing that the constructed measurement assigns
    27	  little state-dependent mass to outcomes outside the encoding image.
    28	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Evaluation of the multilinear
    29	  interpolant is elementary polynomial algebra.  The non-encoding-mass bound
    30	  uses project-specific consistency estimates and Schwartz--Zippel.
    31	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Multilinear interpolation on the
    32	  Boolean cube, injectivity of the low-degree encoding, measurement
    33	  consistency, and Schwartz--Zippel.  The correction is tracked in
    34	  \ghissue{19}.
    35	\end{itemize}
    36	
    37	\section{Key theorem forms}
    38	
    39	For a word $h\colon\{0,1\}^m\to\mathbb F_q$, let $g_h$ be its multilinear
    40	extension.  Define the chapter's decoder by
    41	\[
    42	  \operatorname{Dec}(g)(y)=g(y),
    43	  \qquad y\in\{0,1\}^m.
    44	\]
    45	Then
    46	\[
    47	  \operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h
    48	  \quad\text{and}\quad
    49	  \operatorname{Dec}(g_h)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)=g_h(u).
    50	\]
    51	More generally, the second identity holds for a polynomial outcome $g$ under
    52	the explicit hypothesis that $g$ belongs to the image of the encoding; no
    53	converse is asserted.
    54	
    55	For an arbitrary bounded individual-degree polynomial $g$, the Boolean values
    56	determine its multilinear interpolant, not necessarily $g$ itself.  The
    57	unrestricted identity
    58	\[
    59	  \operatorname{Dec}(g)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)=g(u)
    60	\]
    61	is therefore false.
    62	
    63	\section{Counterexample and source comparison}
    64	
    65	The low-degree encoding is defined at lines~873--897 of
    66	\path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex}.  The general decoder at
    67	lines~917--924 retains evaluations lying in a chosen subset $H$; the extraction
    68	chapter instead specifies at lines~1419--1420 of
    69	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} that the
    70	decoder returns all evaluations on the Boolean cube.  This is the specialization
    71	$H=\mathbb F_q$, rather than the Boolean-valued shorthand used earlier
    72	\cite[lines~873--924 and 1419--1420]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
    73	
    74	Take $m=1$, $d\geq2$, and a field of characteristic two with more than two
    75	elements.  For $g(x)=x^2$, the Boolean evaluations are $g(0)=0$ and $g(1)=1$.
    76	Consequently the decoder is the word whose multilinear extension is $x$.
    77	For any $u\notin\{0,1\}$ with $u^2\neq u$,
    78	\[
    79	  \operatorname{Dec}(g)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_1(u)=u
    80	  \neq u^2=g(u).
    81	\]
    82	Thus the equality asserted for every $g$ at lines~1483--1492 of the chapter-14
    83	source mirror is false \cite[lines~1483--1492]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  If degrees at
    84	least $q$ are allowed, equality as a function would not by itself prove encoding
    85	membership either, since $x^q$ and $x$ induce the same function on $\mathbb F_q$.
    86	
    87	\section{Required repair}
    88	
    89	The extraction proof must split the marginal measurement into encoding and
    90	non-encoding outcomes.  On encoding outcomes, the restricted identity above
    91	justifies the substitution.  On the complement, the proof must bound
    92	\[
    93	  \sum_{g\ \mathrm{not\ an\ encoding}}
    94	  \langle\widehat\psi,\widehat S_g^W\widehat\psi\rangle.
    95	\]
    96	The blueprint derives an $O(\delta_S)+md/q$ bound from point consistency and
    97	the combined point measurement.  A non-encoding polynomial differs from every
    98	encoded polynomial, so Schwartz--Zippel bounds the probability that their
    99	evaluations coincide.  This estimate is the open reduction; it must be proved
   100	from the paper hypotheses rather than inserted as an extraction hypothesis.
   101	
   102	The printed reindexing at lines~1805--1822 replaces
   103	$g_{\operatorname{Dec}(g_W)}$ by $g_W$, which is the invalid reverse identity
   104	for an arbitrary polynomial outcome.  In the corrected calculation, the
   105	constraint is
   106	$g_h(u)=\operatorname{Dec}(g_W)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)-a$.
   107	After setting $h'=h+\operatorname{Dec}(g_W)$, the defining evaluation formula
   108	$g_k(u)=k\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)$ and characteristic two turn
   109	that constraint into $g_{h'}(u)=a$.  Thus this step uses neither decoder
   110	linearity nor the identity $\operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h$
   111	\cite[lines~1805--1822]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   112	
   113	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   114	
   115	Definition~\path{def:qld-full-field-decoder} and
   116	Lemmas~\path{lem:qld-decoder-linearity} and
   117	\path{lem:qld-decoder-evaluation} in
   118	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} state the full-field
   119	decoder, its linearity and inverse, and the evaluation identity restricted to
   120	encoding outcomes.  Lemma~\path{lem:qld-nonencoding-mass-bound}
   121	separately records the estimate on the remaining outcomes.
   122	
   123	The declarations \path{decodeFq_add}, \path{decodeFq_smul}, and
   124	\path{decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding} in
   125	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Decoding.lean} match the three algebraic assertions.
   126	In the same file, \path{IsEncoding} is the equality
   127	$g_{\operatorname{Dec}(g)}=g$ of polynomial representatives, and
   128	\path{decodeFq_dotProduct_indicatorVec} requires an explicit hypothesis
   129	of that predicate.  It therefore matches the corrected evaluation lemma and
   130	does not assert the false unrestricted identity.  Finally,

   132	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/Consistency.lean} concludes the complementary
   133	mass bound from the projective strategy and global polynomial-pair witness; it
   134	does not add the bound as a witness field or theorem hypothesis.
   135	
   136	These proposition-valued declarations are present with open proofs.  Issue~\#19
   137	owns their Stage~4.2 statements and this discrepancy record; \ghissue{47} owns
   138	the Stage~4.3 decoder calculations and non-encoding support estimate.  No
   139	unrestricted theorem, residual assumption, or additional witness field is
   140	source-faithful.
   141	
   142	\section{Conclusion}
   143	
   144	The decoding identity is false for a general polynomial outcome.  Restricting
   145	it to the encoding image is a necessary local correction.  Recovering the
   146	source's measurement-consistency conclusion then requires the separate
   147	non-encoding-mass estimate, which remains an open proof obligation.

The proofs require the latter reading, $H = \F_q$, which is adopted throughout this chapter: the linearity of $\mathrm{Dec}$ and the identity $\mathrm{Dec}(g_h) = h$ for all $h \in \F_q^{M}$, both of which fail for the boolean map, are used in the symmetry step of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} and in the conjugation identity \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6}. The source further asserts the identity $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = g(u)$ for every $g \in \mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$. Since the left-hand side equals $g_{\mathrm{Dec}(g)}(u)$, the identity, taken for all $u \in \F_q^m$, states that the multilinear representative $g_{\mathrm{Dec}(g)}$ and $g$ induce the same function on $\F_q^m$. Every encoding satisfies it, because then $g_{\mathrm{Dec}(g)} = g$ as polynomial representatives; a polynomial that is not an encoding need not: for $m = 1$, $d \geq 2$, and $q > 2$, the polynomial $g(x) = x^2$ has $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_1(u) = u$, which differs from $g(u) = u^2$ at every $u \notin \{0,1\}$. When $d \leq q-1$ the failure at some $u$ characterizes the polynomials that are not encodings, since evaluation is injective on representatives of individual degree at most $q-1$ (Definition~\ref{def:polynomials-degree}); when $d \geq q$ it does not: for the admissible tuple $(q,m,d) = (8,1,8)$, the polynomial $g(x) = x^8$ is not an encoding, yet $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_1(u) = u = u^8 = g(u)$ for every $u \in \F_8$.     29	noncomputable def padWithZeros {ι κ : Type*}
    30	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] {n : ℕ}
    31	    (e : κ ≃ ι × (Fin n → Bool)) :
    32	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κ := by
    33	  let L : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κ :=
    34	    { toFun := fun ψ => (EuclideanSpace.equiv κ ℂ).symm fun j =>
    35	        if (e j).2 = 0 then (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e j).1 else 0
    36	      map_add' := by
    37	        intro ψ φ
    38	        apply (EuclideanSpace.equiv κ ℂ).injective
    39	        change (fun j => if (e j).2 = 0 then
    40	          (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ (ψ + φ)) (e j).1 else 0) = _
    41	        ext j
    42	        simp only [map_add, Pi.add_apply]
    43	        split_ifs with h <;> simp [h]
    44	      map_smul' := by
    45	        intro c ψ
    46	        apply (EuclideanSpace.equiv κ ℂ).injective
    47	        change (fun j => if (e j).2 = 0 then
    48	          (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ (c • ψ)) (e j).1 else 0) = _
    49	        ext j
    50	        simp only [map_smul, Pi.smul_apply]
    51	        split_ifs with h <;> simp [h] }
    52	  refine { toLinearMap := L, norm_map' := fun ψ => ?_ }
    53	  apply (sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).mp
    54	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
    55	  change (∑ j : κ, ‖if (e j).2 = 0 then ψ (e j).1 else 0‖ ^ 2) = _
    56	  change (∑ j : κ, (fun p : ι × (Fin n → Bool) =>
    57	    ‖if p.2 = 0 then ψ p.1 else 0‖ ^ 2) (e j)) = _
    58	  calc
    59	    _ = ∑ p : ι × (Fin n → Bool),
    60	        ‖if p.2 = 0 then ψ p.1 else 0‖ ^ 2 := e.sum_comp _
    61	    _ = _ := by
    62	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    63	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    64	      intro i _
    65	      rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (0 : Fin n → Bool)]

    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Low.  The source drops a nontrivial phase when the
    23	  two binary-basis indices are distinct.
    24	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} One exact multiplication calculation for
    25	  generalized Pauli observables; no robustness estimate changes.
    26	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Finite-sum bilinearity and the field
    27	  trace are standard algebra.  The extracted-observable product form and the
    28	  project's phase convention are project-local.
    29	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} The generalized Pauli commutation
    30	  relation and nondegeneracy of the trace pairing.  The local correction is
    31	  tracked in \ghissue{19}.
    32	\end{itemize}
    33	
    34	\section{Key theorem forms}
    35	
    36	Let $e_0,\ldots,e_{t-1}$ be the fixed self-dual basis of $\mathbb F_q$ over
    37	$\mathbb F_2$.  With the phase convention of the source, generalized Pauli
    38	observables satisfy
    39	\[
    40	  \tau^X(a)\tau^Z(b)
    41	  =(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(a\mathbin{\cdot}b)}
    42	   \tau^Z(b)\tau^X(a).
    43	\]
    44	Substituting $a=e_j\widetilde u$ and $b=e_{j'}\widetilde v$ gives the exact
    45	relation
    46	\[
    47	  \widetilde X^j(\widetilde u)\widetilde Z^{j'}(\widetilde v)
    48	  =(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}
    49	      (e_je_{j'}(\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v))}
    50	   \widetilde Z^{j'}(\widetilde v)\widetilde X^j(\widetilde u).
    51	\]
    52	This formula applies uniformly, whether or not $j=j'$.
    53	
    54	\section{The false dichotomy in the source}
    55	
    56	Lines~1438--1450 of
    57	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    58	identify each extracted observable with a tensor product containing
    59	$\tau^W(e_j\widetilde u)$.  Lines~1451--1456 then claim that the extracted
    60	$X$- and $Z$-observables commute whenever $j\neq j'$
    61	\cite[lines~1438--1456]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  Self-duality gives only
    62	\[
    63	  \operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'})=0 \qquad (j\neq j').
    64	\]
    65	It does not imply
    66	\[
    67	  \operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'}s)=0
    68	  \qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathbb F_q.
    69	\]
    70	
    71	Indeed, for distinct $j,j'$, the element $c=e_je_{j'}$ is nonzero.  The trace
    72	pairing is nondegenerate, so there is an $s\in\mathbb F_q$ for which
    73	$\operatorname{tr}(cs)=1$.  Taking vectors whose first coordinates are $1$
    74	and $s$, with all remaining coordinates zero, gives
    75	$\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v=s$.  The two extracted observables
    76	then anticommute.  This is a counterexample to the printed cross-basis
    77	commutation assertion.
    78	
    79	When $\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v$ lies in the prime field, the
    80	printed distinction is recovered from self-duality.  The chapter quantifies
    81	over arbitrary vectors, however, so that special case does not repair its
    82	statement.
    83	
    84	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
    85	
    86	Equation~\path{eq:tildew-twisted-commutation} and
    87	Remark~\path{rem:qld-cross-phase} in

    96	blueprint and deliberately differs from the false cross-basis commutation
    97	claim in the paper; it introduces no extra hypothesis.

    99	The declaration is present but its proof remains open.  Issue~\#19 owns the

   102	
   103	This correction changes neither the definition of the extracted observables
   104	nor the source-faithful consistency and extraction conclusions.  It repairs an
   105	auxiliary algebraic assertion that is independent of the robustness estimates.
   106	
   107	\section{Conclusion}
   108	
   109	The source's cross-basis commutation claim is false for general
   110	$\widetilde u$ and $\widetilde v$.  The correct relation retains the phase
   111	$(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'}(\widetilde u\cdot\widetilde v))}$.
   112	Because the later argument does not invoke the false dichotomy, this is a
   113	local correction rather than an additional hypothesis on the extraction

    36	the register type. This is the index set of `def:expanded-state`; blueprint
    37	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    38	noncomputable instance sixRegDecidableEq (P : AdmissibleParams)
    39	    (ιA ιB : Type*) : DecidableEq (SixReg P ιA ιB) :=
    40	  Classical.decEq _
    41	
    42	/-- Reassociate the tensor product of the strategy state and two EPR states
    43	directly into register order `AA'A''BB'B''` for
    44	`eq:def-psihat`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`. -/
    45	def sixRegShuffle (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    46	    (((ιA × ιB) × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
    47	        (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ≃ SixReg P ιA ιB where
    48	  toFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    49	    (p.1.1.2, (p.2.1, p.2.2)))
    50	  invFun p := (((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    51	    (p.2.2.1, p.2.2.2))
    52	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    53	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    54	
    55	/-- The four placements `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, and `AB''` used explicitly in
    56	the chapter-14 consistency statements. Paper
    57	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`; blueprint
    58	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
    59	inductive Placement where
    60	  | AA'
    61	  | BA''
    62	  | BB'
    63	  | AB''
    64	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    65	
    66	/-- The strategy-player side supplying the local Hilbert space in each of the
    67	four register placements at paper
    68	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`. -/
    69	def Placement.side : Placement → PlayerSide
    70	  | .AA' => .alice
    71	  | .BA'' => .bob
    72	  | .BB' => .bob
    73	  | .AB'' => .alice
    74	
    75	namespace ProjectiveSetting
    76	
    77	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    78	
    79	/-- A strategy-local register paired with one generalized-Pauli register. This
    80	is the operator space in `def:expanded-observables`, paper
    81	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:374-382`. -/
    82	abbrev ExpandedLocalSpace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :=
    83	  S.LocalSpace side × PauliRegister P
    84	
    85	/-- The strategy state tensored with EPR states on `A'A''` and `B'B''`, in the
    86	six-register order. This is `eq:def-psihat`, paper
    87	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`, blueprint
    88	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    89	noncomputable def psiHat (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
    90	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
    91	  classical
    92	  exact
    93	    reindexState (sixRegShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    94	      (vecTensor
    95	        (vecTensor S.toStrategy.ψ (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    96	        (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    97	
    98	/-- Place an operator on one of `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, or `AB''`, with the
    99	identity on all remaining registers. The input local space is determined by
   100	the placement, so no equality between the player spaces is assumed. Paper
   101	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`; blueprint
   102	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
   103	noncomputable def place (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
   104	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
   105	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   106	  fun i j =>
   107	    match p with
   108	    | .AA' =>
   109	        O (i.1.1, i.1.2.1) (j.1.1, j.1.2.1) *
   110	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   111	          (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) i.2.1 j.2.1 *
   112	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1 *
   113	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   114	    | .BA'' =>
   115	        (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) i.1.1 j.1.1 *
   116	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   117	          O (i.2.1, i.1.2.2) (j.2.1, j.1.2.2) *
   118	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1 *
   119	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   120	    | .BB' =>
   121	        (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) i.1.1 j.1.1 *
   122	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   123	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   124	          O (i.2.1, i.2.2.1) (j.2.1, j.2.2.1) *
   125	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   126	    | .AB'' =>
   127	        O (i.1.1, i.2.2.2) (j.1.1, j.2.2.2) *
   128	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   129	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   130	          (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) i.2.1 j.2.1 *
   131	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1
   132	
   133	/-- The expanded observable
   134	`W^r(u) tensor tau^W(r * ind_m(u))` on a selected player side. This is
   135	Equation `eq:lc-23`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:374-382`,
   136	blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:783-807`. -/
   137	noncomputable def expObs (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   138	    (W : PauliKind) (r : PauliScalar P) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   139	    Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   140	  heteroKron (S.pointObs side W r u)
   141	    (tauObservable W (fun h => r * indicatorVec u h))
   142	
   143	/-- The Fourier average defining the expanded point effect. This is the first
   144	display of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   145	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`, blueprint
   146	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   147	noncomputable def expPointOp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   148	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   149	    Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   150	  averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (PauliScalar P)) fun r =>
   151	    phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (a * r)) • S.expObs side W r u
   152	
   153	/-- The Pauli-register projector onto labels whose low-degree encoding has
   154	value `a` at `u`. This is Equation `eq:qld-point-obs-def`, paper
   155	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:389-394`, blueprint
   156	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   157	noncomputable def tauPointProj (W : PauliKind)
   158	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Op (PauliRegister P) :=
   159	  ∑ h ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun h : PauliRegister P =>
   160	      dotProduct h (indicatorVec u) = a),
   161	    pauliProj W h
   162	
   163	/-- Expanded point effects are positive semidefinite. This is the positivity
   164	obligation in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   165	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`. -/
   166	theorem expPointOp_nonneg (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   167	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   168	    0 ≤ S.expPointOp side W u a := by
   169	  sorry
   170	
   171	/-- Expanded point effects sum to the identity. This is the completeness
   172	obligation in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   173	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`. -/
   174	theorem expPointOp_sum_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   175	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   176	    ∑ a, S.expPointOp side W u a = 1 := by
   177	  sorry
   178	
   179	/-- The complete expanded point measurement on the chosen player and Pauli
   180	register. Its effects are those of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   181	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`, blueprint
   182	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   183	noncomputable def pointMeasExp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   184	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   185	    Measurement (PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   186	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne (S.expPointOp side W u)
   187	    (S.expPointOp_nonneg side W u) (S.expPointOp_sum_eq_one side W u)
   188	
   189	/-- The expanded point effect is the convolution of the strategy point
   190	measurement and the Pauli-register point projection. This is the final display
   191	of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   192	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:395-418`. -/
   193	theorem expPointOp_eq_convolution (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   194	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   195	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
   196	    S.expPointOp side W u a =
   197	      ∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P =>
   198	          p.1 + p.2 = a),
   199	        heteroKron ((S.pointMeas side W u).effect p.1)
   200	          (tauPointProj W u p.2) := by
   201	  sorry
   202	
   203	/-- The expanded point measurement is projective, as asserted after the
   204	convolution formula in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   205	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:395-418`. -/
   206	theorem pointMeasExp_isProjective (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   207	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   208	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.pointMeasExp side W u) := by
   209	  sorry
   210	
   211	/-- Trace-coarse-graining of the expanded point measurement. This is Equation
   212	`eq:qld-def-mptur`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:411-418`,
   213	blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:846-874`. -/
   214	noncomputable def expPointTrace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   215	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   216	    (r : PauliScalar P) : Measurement (ZMod 2) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   217	  (S.pointMeasExp side W u).postprocess fun a => fixedBinTrace P.model (a * r)
   218	
   219	/-- Fourier inversion writes a trace-coarse-grained point effect as one half
   220	of the identity plus its signed expanded observable. This is Equation
   221	`eq:lc-22`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:411-418`, blueprint
   222	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:846-874`. -/
   223	theorem expPointTrace_eq_half_add (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   224	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   225	    (r : PauliScalar P) (b : ZMod 2) :
   226	    (S.expPointTrace side W u r).effect b =
   227	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ •
   228	        (1 + phaseSign b • S.expObs side W r u) := by
   229	  sorry
   230	
   231	end ProjectiveSetting
   232	
   233	end
   234

     3	/-!
     4	# Finite-dimensional state transformations
     5	
     6	This file defines the tensor and reindexing operations used for strategy
     7	distance, Magic Square rigidity, and the qudit-to-qubit isomorphism. See
     8	blueprint chapters 11--13 and the declaration-level references below.
     9	-/
    10	
    11	open scoped Matrix
    12	
    13	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    14	
    15	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    16	
    17	/-- Conjugation by the local isometries in `thm:ms-rigidity` and
    18	`lem:pauli-binary`; blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244` and
    19	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:710-741`, paper
    20	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-652` and
    21	`04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`. -/
    22	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    23	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    24	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    25	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    26	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
    27	  U * M * Uᴴ
    28	
    29	/-- Coordinate transport used by `def:strategy-distance`, blueprint
    30	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    31	noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    32	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    33	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
    34	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    35	    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))
    36	
    37	/-- Apply the two independent local isometries of `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    38	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244`, paper
    39	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-652`. -/
    40	noncomputable def isometryTensor
    41	    {ιA ιB κA κB : Type*}
    42	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    43	    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
    44	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
    45	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
    46	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    47	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB) :=
    48	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (κA × κB) ℂ).symm
    49	    (fun p =>
    50	      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
    51	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv κA ℂ)
    52	            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
    53	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv κB ℂ)
    54	            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *
    55	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA × ιB) ℂ) ψ (i, j)))
    56	
    57	/-- Coordinate tensor used in the ideal state of `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    58	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244`, paper
    59	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-652`. -/
    60	noncomputable def vecTensor {ι κ : Type*}
    61	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
    62	    (u : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ κ) :
    63	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × κ) :=
    64	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ι × κ) ℂ).symm
    65	    (fun p => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ u) p.1 * (EuclideanSpace.equiv κ ℂ v) p.2)
    66	
    67	/-- Operator transport used by `def:strategy-distance`, blueprint
    68	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    69	def reindexOp {ι ι' : Type*} (e : ι ≃ ι') (M : Op ι') : Op ι :=
    70	  (Matrix.reindex e.symm e.symm) M
    71	
    72	/-- Four-factor tensor shuffle used by `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    73	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244`, paper
    74	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-652`. -/
    75	def prodShuffle {α β γ δ : Type*} :
    76	    (α × β) × (γ × δ) ≃ (α × γ) × (β × δ) where
    77	  toFun p := ((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2, p.2.2))
    78	  invFun p := ((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2, p.2.2))
    79	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    80	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    81	
    82	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     5	/-!

     7

    12	## References
    13	
    14	The declarations formalize `lem:qld-comm-cons` in

    23	noncomputable section
    24	
    25	/-- The four directed cross-party placement pairs asserted by the source's

    29	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
    30	def Placement.IsOpposite : Placement → Placement → Prop
    31	  | .AA', .BA'' => True
    32	  | .BA'', .AA' => True
    33	  | .BB', .AB'' => True
    34	  | .AB'', .BB' => True
    35	  | _, _ => False

    37	/-- The square-root error obtained by the expanded-observable commutation
    38	argument in `lem:qld-comm-cons`, paper
    39	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:475-505`, blueprint
    40	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:932-1032`. -/
    41	noncomputable def deltaAnticom (ε : ℝ) : ℝ :=
    42	  Real.sqrt ε
    43	
    44	/-- The concrete square-root error is polynomially small in the sense used by
    45	chapters 14 and 15. This discharges the error-function part of
    46	`lem:qld-comm-cons`, blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:932-1032`, from the
    47	explicit value proved at paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:503-505`. -/
    48	theorem deltaAnticom_isPolyErr : IsPolyErr deltaAnticom := by

    53	  · rw [deltaAnticom, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow]

    56	/-- All expanded-point conclusions at an abstract error function. The first
    57	conjunct lists the four directed cross-party placements; the second lists all
    58	four same-placement commutation conclusions. This proposition collects the
    59	expanded-point conclusions of `lem:qld-comm-cons`, blueprint

    61	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:452-505`. -/
    62	def ExpandedPointConclusions (δ : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
    63	  (∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
    64	    ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    65	      (p₁ p₂ : Placement), p₁.IsOpposite p₂ →
    66	      ∀ W : PauliKind,

    70	          (fun u a => S.place p₂
    71	            ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side W u).effect a))
    72	          S.psiHat ≤ C * ε) ∧
    73	  (∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
    74	    ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    75	      (p : Placement),
    76	      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PauliTuple P))
    77	        (fun ω (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) => S.place p
    78	          ((S.expPointTrace p.side .X ω.1 ω.2.2.1).effect bits.1 *
    79	            (S.expPointTrace p.side .Z ω.2.1 ω.2.2.2).effect bits.2))
    80	        (fun ω (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) => S.place p
    81	          ((S.expPointTrace p.side .Z ω.2.1 ω.2.2.2).effect bits.2 *
    82	            (S.expPointTrace p.side .X ω.1 ω.2.2.1).effect bits.1))
    83	        S.psiHat ≤ C * δ ε)

    87	parameters and strategies. This is item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-cons`, paper
    88	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:455-465`, blueprint
    89	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:942-959`. -/
    90	theorem expPoint_self_cons :
    91	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
    92	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    93	        (p₁ p₂ : Placement), p₁.IsOpposite p₂ →
    94	        ∀ W : PauliKind,
    95	          opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
    96	            (fun u a => S.place p₁
    97	              ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side W u).effect a))
    98	            (fun u a => S.place p₂
    99	              ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side W u).effect a))
   100	            S.psiHat ≤ C * ε := by
   101	  sorry
   102	
   103	/-- Trace-coarse-grained expanded point projections approximately commute on
   104	each of `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, and `AB''`. The universal constant precedes all
   105	test parameters and strategies. This is item 2 of `lem:qld-comm-cons`, paper
   106	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:466-505`, blueprint
   107	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:960-1032`. -/
   108	theorem expPointTrace_comm :
   109	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
   110	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)

   434	\paragraph{Partitioning the registers, and symmetries}
   435	In the remainder of this section as well as \Cref{sec:combining,sec:apply-ldt}, we will partition the six registers
   436	$\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''$ into
   437	two ``parties'' in two different ways. The first is to consider
   438	$\alice \alice'$ together to form  a single party, and $\bob \alice''$
   439	to form the second party. The second is to consider $\bob \bob'$ to
   440	form the first party, and $\alice \bob''$ to form the second
   441	party. Thanks to the symmetry of the Pauli basis test under exchanging the
   442	two players, as well as the symmetry of the ancilla states in
   443	registers $\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$, every ``bipartite'' consistency relation we derive between two
   444	operators $M, N$ will hold for both of the two bipartitioning schemes,
   445	and with the first and second party interchanged. That is, whenever we
   446	derive a bipartite relation of the form
   447	\[ M_{\alice \alice'} \approx_\delta N_{\bob \alice''}, \]
   448	the same steps, with the registers appropriately changed, will also
   449	yield
   450	\begin{align*}
   451	  N_{\alice \alice'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\bob \alice''}, \\
   452	  M_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} N_{\alice \bob''}, \\
   453	  N_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\alice \bob''}.
   454	\end{align*}
   455	
   456	Similarly, whenever we derive a single-party relation of the form
   457	$M_{\alice \alice'} \approx N_{\alice \alice'}$, the same steps with
   458	the registers appropriately changed will also yield the same relation
   459	on $\bob\alice''$, $\bob \bob'$ and $\alice \bob''$. We refer to these
   460	relations as \emph{symmetric equivalents}.

   115		$\{\mathcal{L}^u\}$ indexed by $u \in \F_2^t$ acting on
   116		$\hilb \ot \hilb'$ such that, writing
   117		$\rho' = \rho \ot \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}$, the exact
   118		linearity

   120			\mathcal{L}^u \, \mathcal{L}^{u'} = \mathcal{L}^{u+u'}
   121		\]
   122		holds for all $u, u' \in \F_2^t$, and
   123		\[
   124			\E_{u} \, d_{\rho'}\big(\mathcal{L}^u,\ \mathcal{O}^u \ot
   125			\Id_{\hilb'}\big)^2 \le \delta\,,
   126		\]
   127		where the expectation is over $u$ chosen uniformly at random from
   128		$\F_2^t$ and
   129		$d_{\sigma}(S,T)
   130		= \big(\Tr\big((S-T)^\dagger (S-T)\, \sigma\big)\big)^{1/2}$

   132		operator $\sigma$.

   136		Vidick~\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}, imported as an external result;
   137		no proof is given in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}, which invokes the result
   138		directly. The verification obligations attached to the import at its
   139		point of use --- the correspondence between the correlation hypothesis
   140		above and the relation $\approx_\delta$ of
   141		Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}, the instantiation of $\rho$ as a
   142		reduced state of $\ket{\hat\psi}$, the absorption of the ancilla
   143		register into padding of the strategy state, and the identity
   144		$\mathcal{L}^0 = \Id$ --- are enumerated in
   145		Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-import} and addressed in the proof of
   146		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}.

   149	\begin{remark}[Obligations of the linearity-theorem import]
   150		\label{rem:linearity-import}
   151		Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} is stated in the form proved in
   152		\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}. Three features are load-bearing for the
   153		proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}: the error is preserved without
   154		polynomial loss ($\delta$ in the hypothesis becomes $\delta$ in the
   155		conclusion); the linearity of the $\{\mathcal{L}^u\}$ is exact and
   156		holds for all pairs $(u,u')$, not merely on average; and the
   157		hypothesis carries no upper bound on $\delta$, so the theorem may be
   158		applied separately for each pair $(x,z)$ with hypothesis error the
   159		conditional linearity defect given $(x,z)$, a quantity for which no a
   160		priori bound is available. The closeness of $\mathcal{L}^u$ to
   161		$\mathcal{O}^u$ is guaranteed on average over a uniformly random $u$
   162		only; this averaged form suffices because the $\mathcal{L}^u$ enter
   163		the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10} only through averages over $u$.
   164		The quotation of the theorem in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} differs from the
   165		cited statement in three respects: it inserts the restriction
   166		$0 \le \delta \le 1$, which would block the fiberwise application
   167		just described; it places the closeness conclusion, together with the
   168		exact linearity, under the quantifier ``for all $u, u' \in \F_2^t$'',
   169		a strengthening of the theorem proved in
   170		\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}; and it appends the identity
   171		$\mathcal{L}^u = \Id$ for $u = 0$. None of the three is reproduced
   172		here: the restriction is dropped, the pointwise closeness is not
   173		used, and the appended identity is instead derived from the
   174		conclusion, since exact linearity at $u = u' = 0$ gives
   175		$(\mathcal{L}^0)^2 = \mathcal{L}^0$, and an idempotent unitary equals
   176		the identity. The import carries two conversion obligations,
   177		discharged in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}: the theorem is
   178		instantiated with $\rho$ the reduced density operator of
   179		$\ket{\hat\psi}$ on the registers carrying the observables, so that
   180		traces against $\rho$ are expectation values in $\ket{\hat\psi}$; and
   181		the correlation hypothesis and the squared-distance conclusion are
   182		converted to and from the relation $\approx_\delta$ of
   183		Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance} by expanding the square, using
   184		unitarity of the observables, and relabelling the averaged index
   185		pair, at the cost of the constant factors absorbed by that
   186		definition. One obligation remains open and is flagged where it
   187		arises: the ancilla register $\hilb'$ and its state

   191		assumes present without construction.

The source further asserts the identity $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = g(u)$ for every $g \in \mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$. Since the left-hand side equals $g_{\mathrm{Dec}(g)}(u)$, the identity, taken for all $u \in \F_q^m$, states that the multilinear representative $g_{\mathrm{Dec}(g)}$ and $g$ induce the same function on $\F_q^m$. Every encoding satisfies it, because then $g_{\mathrm{Dec}(g)} = g$ as polynomial representatives; a polynomial that is not an encoding need not: for $m = 1$, $d \geq 2$, and $q > 2$, the polynomial $g(x) = x^2$ has $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_1(u) = u$, which differs from $g(u) = u^2$ at every $u \notin \{0,1\}$. When $d \leq q-1$ the failure at some $u$ characterizes the polynomials that are not encodings, since evaluation is injective on representatives of individual degree at most $q-1$ (Definition~\ref{def:polynomials-degree}); when $d \geq q$ it does not: for the admissible tuple $(q,m,d) = (8,1,8)$, the polynomial $g(x) = x^8$ is not an encoding, yet $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_1(u) = u = u^8 = g(u)$ for every $u \in \F_8$.
